newsitem.title: USA: US SPOT NATGAS RALLIES WITH FUTURES, STORAGE DATA.
newsitem.headline: US SPOT NATGAS RALLIES WITH FUTURES, STORAGE DATA.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices followed the lead of futures and a lower-than-expected AGA number Thursday, resulting in another 10 cent gain in most markets, sources said.
AGA data showed a weekly stock build of only 55 bcf, bringing inventories to just 133 bcf, or 7.5 percent, above last year's record lows.

On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were quoted up an average of 11-13 cents to about $2.50, with deals reported done anywhere from a high of $2.55 early and a low of $2.37 shortly before nomination deadlines.
In the Midwest, swing prices similarly gained another 14 cents to the low-$2.40s. Chicago city-gate gas prices ranged anywhere from $2.59 to $2.50.
In the Permian Basin market, lingering above-normal temperatures across the West pushed prices about 10 cents higher to $2.40-2.50.

San Juan basin gas was also several cents higher at $2.35-2.45. Southern California border prices rose another 15 cents to the low-$2.60s while some California utilities reported record peak demands due to the heat.
In the East, prices at the New York city gate jumped about 10-15 cents to $2.60-2.70.
